newsitem.title: USA: Vertex says resistance not seen to therapy.
newsitem.headline: Vertex says resistance not seen to therapy.

text.p: Vertex Pharmaceuticals Inc said preliminary data from a four-week clinical study show that resistance did not develop to 141W94/VX-478 HIV protease inhibitor administered as a single agent over that time period.
Vertex said it designed the 141W94/VX-478 inhibitor and it is in development in the United States and Europe by Glaxo Wellcome Plc and in the Far East by Kissei Pharmaceutical Co Ltd.
Vertex said resistance did not appear to develop to 141W94/VX-478 during the Phase I/II study whether at the lower, sub-optimal doses or at higher doses where potent antiviral activity was observed.
Vertex said the data should be interpreted with caution given the short duration of the study.
Vertex also said preliminary data suggest that the combination of the investigational antiretroviral agents, 1592U89 and 141W94/VX-478, is an effective and well tolerated treatment for HIV infection.

Initial results from an ongoing small Phase I/II clinical trial show that five of seven patients treated with the combination of 141W94/VX-478 and 1592U89 for four weeks experienced drops in HIV viral load to below the limits of detection, Vertex said.
The compound 1592U89 is being developed by Glaxo Wellcome.
Early indications suggest this combination is generally well tolerated with nausea being the most commonly reported adverse event with this combination, Vertex said.
